chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān and Ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a believer who intentionally kills another believer: does he have repentance? So he said:

"If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him. But if he killed him out of anger or due to some worldly cause, then his repentance is that retribution be taken from him. If no one knew about it, he should go to the heirs of the slain person and confess before them that he killed their companion. If they pardon him and do not kill him, he must give them the blood money, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons as repentance to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.أَنْ يُقَادَ مِنْهُ: that retribution be taken from him; legal retaliation (qisas)
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal guardians of the slain person
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money paid to the victim’s heirs
key_terms.تَوْبَةٌ: repentance; returning to Allah after grave sin
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months of fasting as expiation
key_terms.لِإِيمَانِهِ: because of his faith; indicating sectarian or religiously motivated killing
key_terms.لِغَضَبٍ: out of anger; a personal motive distinct from hatred of faith
key_terms.نَسَمَةً: a slave person to be freed as expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the repentance for someone who intentionally kills a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between killing a believer out of hostility to faith and killing due to anger or worldly motives. In the latter case, it outlines the legal and penitential consequences: surrendering to qisas if pursued, or otherwise confessing to the victim’s heirs, paying the diyyah if pardoned, and performing expiatory acts as repentance to Allah عزّ وجلّ.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5164 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdullah (as), who was asked about a believer who intentionally kills another believer - does he have repentance?

Imam (as) said: "If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him.
But if he killed him out of anger or due to some worldly reason, then his repentance is that retribution be taken from him.
If no one knows about it, he should go to the family of the murdered person and confess to them that he killed their relative. If they forgive him and do not kill him, he must give them the blood money (diyyah), free a slave, fast for two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy people as repentance to Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic."
